deep.reconstruction:
The page has two layers: a printed page (p. 82) from a German elementary algebra textbook of about 1790–1800, and Gauss's handwritten marginal calculations on the right edge, which are partly cut off.

(A) PRINTED TEXT (not by Gauss).
- §174 (end): an equation is 'zusammengesetzt' (compound, i.e. nonlinear) if the unknown appears in a higher power, as a divisor, as a factor of another unknown, or under a root sign.
- Example, continuing the previous page (x+y=20 with solution x=16, y=4). Several different set-ups all lead to a quadratic:
  (i) y^2 = x or y = sqrt(x) gives y^2 + y = 20, so y = 4 (or -5), x = 16.
  (ii) 64/y = x gives 64/y + y = 20, so y^2 - 20y + 64 = 0 and y = 4 or 16.
  (iii) xy = 64 with x = 20 - y gives (20 - y)y = 64, the same quadratic.
  (iv) log y = (1/2) log x gives y = x^(1/2) = sqrt(x), as in (i).
  The book calls all of these quadratic because y rises to the 2nd power, and says they all give 'the same values' x=16, y=4.
- §175: a 'pure' equation has the form x^m = A. An 'impure' one is complete if all lower powers occur, incomplete otherwise.
- §176: 'ordering' an equation means (1) collecting terms of equal power (reducing), then (2) putting the highest power, with + sign, first, the next power second, and so on.

(B) GAUSS'S MARGINALIA.
They continue the margin of p. 81 (which ends with 36·41/(720·7) = 41/140) and are fair-copied on p. 83. Gauss is computing the closed Newton–Cotes weights for 7 equidistant nodes t = 0,…,6 (step h = 1). Each weight is the integral over [0,6] of the Lagrange basis polynomial.

The three fragments headed 'Corr' (Correction?) are drafts of:

1. Weight of node 1 (β, = node 5, ζ):
   - w1 = -(1/120) ∫_0^6 t(t-2)(t-3)(t-4)(t-5)(t-6) dt.
   - The polynomial expands to t^6 - 20t^5 + 155t^4 - 580t^3 + 1044t^2 - 720t.
   - So w1 = -(6^7/7 - 20·6^6/6 + 155·6^5/5 - 580·6^4/4 + 1044·6^3/3 - 720·6^2/2)/120.
   - Factoring out 6^4: the bracket is 6^4(30 6/7 - 120 + 186 - 145 + 58 - 10) = -6^4/7.
   - Hence w1 = 1296/840 = 54/35 = 216/140.
   - The marginal '6^4( 3… 18…' are the cut-off entries 30 6/7 and 186.

2. Weight of node 2 (γ, = node 4, ε):
   - w2 = (1/48) ∫_0^6 t(t-1)(t-3)(t-4)(t-5)(t-6) dt.
   - The polynomial is t^6 - 19t^5 + 137t^4 - 461t^3 + 702t^2 - 360t.
   - The bracket is 6^4(30 6/7 + 164 2/5 + 39 - 114 - 115 1/4 - 5) = 6^4(234 9/35 - 234 1/4) = 6^4/140.
   - Hence w2 = 1296/(140·48) = 27/140.

3. Weight of node 3 (δ):
   - w3 = -(1/36) ∫_0^6 t(t-1)(t-2)(t-4)(t-5)(t-6) dt.
   - The polynomial is t^6 - 18t^5 + 121t^4 - 372t^3 + 508t^2 - 240t.
   - The bracket is 6^3(185 1/7 + 871 1/5 + 169 1/3 - 648 - 558 - 20) = 6^3(1225 71/105 - 1226) = -6^3·34/105.
   - Hence w3 = 6·34/105 = 204/105 = 272/140.
   - The marginal '= [-6^3-]' matches the struck-out first attempt at this factoring on p. 83.

4. Check (bottom margin, 'Est autem'):
   - 82 + 432 + 54 + 272 = 840 = 2·41 + 2·216 + 2·27 + 272.
   - This equals 6·140, as it must, since the weights sum to the interval length 6.

Result: ∫_0^{6h} f ≈ (h/140)[41 f0 + 216 f1 + 27 f2 + 272 f3 + 27 f4 + 216 f5 + 41 f6], the 6-panel closed Newton–Cotes rule.
errors: Printed text: the claim that all set-ups give 'einerley Werth' ignores the second roots. y^2 + y = 20 also has y = -5, and y^2 - 20y + 64 = 0 also has y = 16 (with x = 4); only y = 4, x = 16 is common to all.
Printed text: log y = (1/2) log x is not itself a quadratic; it only yields y = sqrt(x), which together with x + y = 20 gives the quadratic.

Gauss's own drafts contain corrected slips, visible as strike-outs on p. 83: in the γ coefficient he first wrote 156 and 579 for the t^4 and t^3 coefficients, corrected to 137 and 461. In the β coefficient, 889 was corrected to 1044. A first factoring attempt for δ was struck out. The final values 216/140, 27/140 and 272/140 are all correct.

results.what: Classification of equations (simple/compound, pure/impure, complete/incomplete) and ordering of polynomial equations; quadratic example x+y=20, xy=64
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-century textbook material (author of the printed book)

results.what: Computation of the weights 41, 216, 27, 272, 27, 216, 41 (/140) for 7-point equidistant quadrature by integrating Lagrange basis polynomials, with sum check 840 = 6·140

deep.surprise_reason: The printed text is a routine textbook. Gauss's marginalia recompute the known Cotes coefficients for 7 nodes. Gauss explicitly treated and tabulated the Cotes formulas in 'Methodus nova integralium valores per approximationem inveniendi' (1814), so this is essentially a working draft of known material.

transcription_corrections: Printed line 4: 'des vorigen 9.' in the image is the section sign: 'des vorigen §.'
Margin '6^4( 3 / 18' are the truncated entries 30 6/7 and 186 of the beta-coefficient bracket (cf. p. 83).
Margin '= [-6^3-]' is the start of the struck-out first factoring attempt for the delta coefficient.
On p. 83 the factor written '6(' in the delta computation should be read as 6^3( (185 1/7 = 6^4/7 etc. only make sense with 6^3 factored out).
'Corr' at the margin heads is probably an abbreviation (Corr[ection]?); the reading is uncertain because it is cut off.
